meaning: Each tie names the phrase of the paper that a Lean declaration states, as read side by side for Proof Reader (wcook04/proof-reader 3858afbe00b2, papers/navier-stokes-library-24). Titles, reading notes, topics and comparisons are AI-drafted or AI-assessed; no mathematician has reviewed them.

families.name: From a certificate to a profile
From cell data to the certificate

topics.name: The blow-up statements
topics.description: Smooth solutions, breakdown on space and on the torus, and the theorems that state them (Theorem 1.1, Theorem 7.1).

topics.name: The fractional extension
topics.description: The authors' separate extension with dissipation exponent between 1 and 5/4, outside the classical paper.

topics.name: Heat flow and mild solutions
topics.description: The heat semigroup, the bilinear Duhamel term, mild solutions, restarting and uniqueness (§3).

topics.name: Recurrent profiles
topics.description: Self-similar time-periodic profiles, their slices and orbits, and weak profiles read as physical fields (§2, §4.1, §7.11).

topics.name: Monodromy and the correction
topics.description: The period map, its compact-plus-small splitting, the spectral projection and the fixed point that corrects a profile to an exact solution (§4).

topics.name: Passing to the torus
topics.description: The solenoidal cutoff, periodization and the periodic right inverse that move the construction onto the torus (§5–6).

topics.name: From certificate to profile
topics.description: Certificate data, the free operator, convection, held solutions and the smoothing of the weak profile they produce (§7).

topics.name: The coercive multiplier estimate
topics.description: The multiplier, its five density coefficients and lower bound, and the a priori estimate it gives (Appendix B.1 and B.2).

topics.name: Encoded cell data
topics.description: The finitely represented inputs: coordinates and harmonics, the profile representation, splines and jets, physical cells, rows, weights and potentials.

topics.name: Reduction to the quarter plane
topics.description: Symmetry reduction of the density to the meridian quarter plane (B.3).

topics.name: Cells, traces and tails
topics.description: Integrability, the common vector of unknowns, resolved modes, the tail budget and the exterior estimate (B.4).

topics.name: Angular and ray-exterior tests
topics.description: The angular inequalities, the pointwise test and the integrated test on ray exteriors (B.5 and B.6).

topics.name: The matrix tree lower bound
topics.description: The tree conditions on the cell matrices and the passage from all cells to the global inequality (B.7 and B.8).

topics.name: Changing the profile
topics.description: Bounds for moving estimates from the reference field to the actual profile (B.9).

topics.name: The adjoint pairing and its error
topics.description: The quadratic adjoint pairing, the azimuthal dual norm and the linear adjoint error with potentials and pins (B.10 to B.12).

topics.name: The offset and the certificate
topics.description: Enclosing the constant, linear and quadratic offset, and the fifteen fields of CellSystemCondition that make the data a certificate (B.13 and B.14).

notes.Breakdown.FracCert.HasAllMoments: The quantifier starts at homogeneous order one; this definition alone does not supply an order-zero L2 norm.
notes.Breakdown.FracCert.SmoothMomentStepSymbo: The admissibility guard deliberately handles exceptional representatives; later almost-everywhere admissibility results justify agreement with the ordinary annular restriction.
notes.Breakdown.FracCert.symbolX: The reciprocal at frequency zero is Lean's total inverse, so the value there is defined without a nonzero-frequency hypothesis.
notes.Breakdown.SteadyCert.GradientOrthogonalS: This declaration defines a proposition; the separate provider theorem proves that proposition.
notes.Breakdown.SteadyCert.Internal.SecondSymb: The conversion to L² is total and uses zero outside L²; the energy and pairing results separately supply membership hypotheses, so this definition alone asserts no regularity of an arbitrary input.
notes.Breakdown.SteadyCert.StiffEnclosureInter: The bound is the Euclidean triangle inequality written for squared finite sums.
notes.Breakdown.SteadyCert.fieldSymbol: The conversion to L² is total and uses zero outside L²; the energy and pairing results separately supply membership hypotheses, so this definition alone asserts no regularity of an arbitrary input.
notes.Breakdown.SteadyCert.fracCertificate_pro: This implication explicitly takes both bridge propositions and the certificate hypothesis as arguments; it does not itself construct numerical certificate data, and the fractional result is outside the ordinary-dissipation paper claim.
notes.Breakdown.SteadyCert.secondSymbol: The conversion to L² is total and uses zero outside L²; the energy and pairing results separately supply membership hypotheses, so this definition alone asserts no regularity of an arbitrary input.
notes.Breakdown.SteadyCert.weakPowerLimit_hold: The velocity limit is recovered as the radial factor times the weak L2 limit of the inverse-radial-weighted velocities.

ties.from: **Convolution integrates f(w)k(x−w).** Proved result `kernelConv_eq`: Kernel convolution at x equals ∫f(w)k(x−w) dw.
ties.to: **Convolution integrates f(w)k(x−w).** Proved result `kernelConv_eq`: Kernel convolution at x equals ∫f(w)k(x−w) dw.

ties.from: **Power bounds for near-field pieces.** Proved result `near_bound`: Under the stated hypotheses, near-field dyadic pieces have power bounds.
ties.to: **Power bounds for near-field pieces.** Proved result `near_bound`: Under the stated hypotheses, near-field dyadic pieces have power bounds.

ties.from: **Far bounds complete the piece estimate.** Proved result `dyadicPieceBound_of_far`: Under the stated assumptions, this establishes that for a nonnegative homogeneous degree d and a weighted smooth input of exponent 0<β<3, the nth derivative of each dyadic convolution obeys the stated near-region bound 2^((d+n+β)l) and the two explicit far-region power bounds for ‖x‖≥2.
ties.to: **Far bounds complete the piece estimate.** Proved result `dyadicPieceBound_of_far`: Under the stated assumptions, this establishes that for a nonnegative homogeneous degree d and a weighted smooth input of exponent 0<β<3, the nth derivative of each dyadic convolution obeys the stated near-region bound 2^((d+n+β)l) and the two explicit far-region power bounds for ‖x‖≥2.

ties.from: **Comparable radii have comparable weights.** Proved result `weight_shift`: For nonnegative radii a and b with 1+b≤2(1+a), the decay weights satisfy (1+a)⁻⁴≤16(1+b)⁻⁴.
ties.to: **Comparable radii have comparable weights.** Proved result `weight_shift`: For nonnegative radii a and b with 1+b≤2(1+a), the decay weights satisfy (1+a)⁻⁴≤16(1+b)⁻⁴.

ties.to: **Convolution derivatives reach the kernel.** Proved result `conv_iteratedFDeriv`: Under the stated hypotheses, convolution derivatives act on the kernel.

ties.from: **Inverse powers compare by scale.** Proved result `rpow_neg_four_le`: If a, b and c are positive and b≤ca, then a⁻⁴≤c⁴b⁻⁴; this transfers a fourth-order decay estimate between comparable distances.
ties.to: **Inverse powers compare by scale.** Proved result `rpow_neg_four_le`: If a, b and c are positive and b≤ca, then a⁻⁴≤c⁴b⁻⁴; this transfers a fourth-order decay estimate between comparable distances.
